summary: ```# Marvelous Designer Official Tutorial: Nurse Uniform Production ## Introduction Hello friends of Marvelous Designer, welcome to this tutorial. Today, we will be creating a nurse uniform using Marvelous Designer. ## Importing the Virtual Model First, we need to import a virtual model. Here, we import Feifei. Then, click on the **Modular Configurator** to switch to the module configurator. ### Accessing Shirt Modules Open the **Women** folder and then open the **Shirts** folder. Double-click on the short sleeve shirt icon; there will be modules in various parts at the bottom. Double-click on the modules to import them. In the Modular Configurator, you can import modules to create all kinds of costumes. If you want to change the model of a module, you only need to double-click on another model to replace it. Please follow the video description for more information. ## Changing Virtual Model Position In the Modular Configurator, select these modules. Switch the module window to the **Library** window and open the **Avata** folder. Since all the preview modules are done in a vertical position, we need to change the virtual model's position to match them. ### Re-activating the Costume File Re-activate the costume file; we will change the position. Open the **Female V2** folder under the **Pose** folder. Download the vertical position file and select default settings. Since we have re-activated the costume, when we change the position, the costume will not participate in the simulation together. After the action is changed, we can activate the shirt. ## Simulating the Shirt Open the simulation and put the shirt on the virtual model. To make it easier to edit the costume, we need to re-apply the symmetrical edit relationship to the version. Before that, we need to remove the module relationship. ### Adjusting the Module Relationship Select the module frame with the adjustment version tool, then press the **Delete** button to remove the module relationship. Then, select all the panels and press the **Right** button to select the panel. In the pop-up menu, select **Unite** so that the panels return to the time when there is no symmetrical relationship. ## Creating Internal Lines Use the internal multidirectional line tool to create the back and middle lines of the body panels to cut the panels in half. Please use these straight lines to create the internal lines. In the pop-up menu, select the **Cut Line** option. In the pop-up menu, select the **Cut Seam** option. After that, select all panels other than the collar. In the pop-up menu, select the **Symmetrical Panel, Panel and Seam** function at the bottom of the link panel option. Now the panel line is displayed as dark blue, and the symmetry relationship has been set. ### Editing Seam Lines Switch to the **Edit Seam** tool; you will see that the seam line is also automatically symmetrical. Then select the **Cut Seam** option. Next, select the seam line between the top and bottom of the back and bottom. In the right-click menu, select **Merge** to merge the panels. Then, switch to the **Edit Panel** tool. Select the straight line on the back and middle lines, press the **Delete** button to delete it. This will make the back and middle become a straight line. Select the back panel, and then select the **Rotation Y-axis** in the right-click menu. Click the back and middle straight line to rotate the panel to the correct position. ## Panel Adjustments Now we will be in the panel section. Open the panel to create a seam line to make the clothing more suitable for the model. Select the seam tool and click on the level on the side of the waist to make the seam line the widest position. After pressing the mouse button, you can enter the specific number of the seam line. Set the width of the left and right sides to 10mm. View the seam line to ensure that it does not exceed the vertical position of the shoulder point on the inside side, and confirm to create a seam line. The seam line is actually a zero-shaped hole, and the line on both sides will automatically create a seam line. ## Final Adjustments on the Shirt Open the model; you will see that the shirt is more suitable than before. Switch to the back view to perform the same operation on the back. Check the wearing effect; now the back seems to be not tight enough. You can tighten it a little more using the adjustment panel tool to select a seam line. The point that drags the seam line on both sides will be widened. If you directly increase the width, the center position of the seam line will be changed along with it. Therefore, we need to use the center point function. Double-click the center point of the seam line; the center point that changes color with the point is activated. At this time, when we drag the point of the seam line to modify the shape, use the center point position as a fixed center to modify. After simulation, after confirming the effect is appropriate, we will add a long shirt to make it into a skirt. ## Editing the Skirt Use the edit panel tool to select all the seam lines. Then drag these lines while pressing the **Shift** key to move them along the vertical direction. When dragging the seam line, double-click to enter the specific vertical. Open the simulation; you will find that the skirt is a little tight near the buttocks. Move the point on the side of the skirt to make the lower part of the skirt wider. When moving the point, press the **Shift** key to open the reference line and level it. Move the bottom and side points of the front and back slices to the outside 40mm to modify the application. Now that the size of the clothes is appropriate, we will adjust the throat part to make it more natural. The upper and lower ends of this throat are a bit out of place, like poking out. We can move the bottom point of the throat down a little to make the part of the throat that was dug out more natural. Do the same on the back. ## Creating the Cut Line Now we will turn the throat into a part of the cut line. Use the internal multilinear line tool to draw the internal line on the outside of the cut line from the upper and lower ends of the throat. Press the **Ctrl** key and click to create a curve point in order to turn the internal line into a curve. Double-click to complete the creation. Then, on the back of the 3D window, click on the position near the internal line as a reference. Go to the blue reference point and start drawing the starting point, then connect to the endpoint of the throat. Complete the creation of the rest of the internal line. ### Final Adjustments to the Cut Line Use the editor tool to select the internal line, then select **Cut and Sew**. Press the **Shift** key and select the two internal lines connecting the throat, then select **Cut and Sew**. The plate will be cut into two separate plates. After opening the simulation, you will find that the cut position is not very smooth. Let's adjust the depth of the throat to make the angle more natural. Move this point of the throat to both sides to make the angle a little bit flatter. Do the same for the other point of the throat. ## Smoothing Edges and Finalizing the Design When the clothing effect is suitable, we use the deepening round-shaped curve tool to turn the excess corner into a round corner. When you switch to the deepening round-shaped curve tool, click on the excess corner to turn it into a round corner. Similarly, you can find the longer point, which can be made on the bottom of a support. In addition, there are some bumps near the support point, which we can adjust with the adjustment tool or the ruler tool. Set the shrink rate to 1% to slightly shrink the position of the brush. Click on the part of the brush to apply the shrink effect, then simulate to check the effect. Now it's flat. Rotate the view to see if there are other places that need to be adjusted. Set the brush size to be smaller to take the shrink position more accurately. The throat on the back is also operated in the same way. ## Final Adjustments and Simulation Now, let's modify the sewing line. Use the editor sewing line tool to move the end point of the sewing line to the end point of the line. After the simulation, you will see that the bottom of the shirt has changed to a flat line. Change to the editor sewing line tool; we will adjust the sewing line. Delete the straight line point and turn the whole bottom into a horizontal line. Drag the bottom down a little; you will find that the side line is curved. To keep the side as a straight line, we need to delete the curve point. ### Adjusting the Sleeve Length After selecting the weight, select the single selection of the line and delete all the curve points. Change the sleeve to be longer. Now the sleeve is a little too wide, and we need to adjust it. We will use the extension tool to keep the seam line unchanged and make the sleeve narrower. Click on the highest point of the sleeve to start creating an extension line. Press the **Shift** key to create an extension line in the vertical direction. Click to complete the creation of the extension line. After creating the extension line, the extension line can be modified on both sides at the same time. ## Bubble Sleeve Effect Next, we are going to make the bubble
